source.title: On the influence of over-parameterization in manifold based surrogates and deep neural operators
source.authors: Katiana Kontolati; S. Goswami; M. Shields; G. Karniadakis

record.tranche_reason: The study varies model parameter counts and training-set sizes and measures test relative L2 error, but does so on Brusselator surrogate models rather than reproducing the original studies' methods and settings.
record.gate_note: The text reports model-size sweeps in Figure 4, training-set-size sweeps in Tables 5 and 7, and additional DeepONet architecture comparisons in Table 3. The study does not report an epoch-wise error curve or identify a training-fit interpolation threshold. Noise in several experiments is added to inputs, not labels.
record.test_reason: The study is not framed around double descent. It sweeps parameter count (Fig. 4, Table 3) and training-set size (Tables 5, 7) for m-PCE, DeepONet and FNO surrogates on the Brusselator PDE and reports test relative L2 error. These are its own results in a new setting, and they bear on V1 and V3. They are not a reproduction of the originals, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that modest over-parameterization helps m-PCE generalize in- and out-of-distribution, while aggressive over-parameterization overfits. Even highly over-parameterized DeepONet and FNO generalize better, though the largest DeepONets may need light L2 regularization. Test error falls with more training data for all models in both cases.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares m-PCE, DeepONet, and FNO surrogates on a Brusselator PDE using relative L2 prediction error; it does not reproduce the original studies' model classes, tasks, or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Case and surrogate family affect outcomes; in Case I the m-PCE error depends on parameter count, while DeepONet error decreases across the reported size sweep. Dataset-size trends are reported separately for Case I and Case II.

fits_no_version.finding: At the largest DeepONet widths, L2 regularization with λ=0.0008 removes the slight over-fitting (2.969→2.69%, 3.058→2.71%), while λ=0.001 slightly worsens it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heavily over-parameterized deep operator networks can show mild over-fitting at extreme width that tuned weight decay removes.

fits_no_version.finding: Robustness to added input noise (10–30%) is near-flat for m-PCE and DeepONet; FNO degrades sharply (17–30% error).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-noise robustness of over-parameterized surrogates depends on architecture.

record.problems: The evidence is limited to one physical system with two dynamics cases. The size-scaling curve is shown in a figure without tabulated point values, no training-error interpolation threshold is identified, and no epoch-wise curve is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Four of the twelve individual Table 3 DeepONet architecture/regularization test-error entries are not extracted because the 60-row limit was reached after preserving the full training-set-size tables and eight Table 3 entries. The omitted entries are the remaining four lower-parameter architectures in Section 4.1, Table 3: [128, 150] with [128, 128, 128, 150] (130796 parameters), [128, 150] with [100, 100, 100, 150] (113660 parameters), [64, 150] with [100, 100, 100, 150] (99900 parameters), and [64, 150] with [128, 128, 128, 150] (117036 parameters).

untested.parts: The peak near the interpolation threshold and the first descent. DeepONet/FNO sizes never approach the threshold.
Entire version: no epoch-wise error curves are reported.
DeepONet, FNO, POD- and SA-DeepONet are far from threshold at every N. Case II m-PCE parameter counts are not given, so the threshold cannot be located.
The m-PCE sweep (Fig. 4) has unreadable range and an ambiguous threshold count. No other non-deep model class is swept.
Entire version. Noise is added to inputs, not labels. Regularization is not tested against a threshold peak.
Entire version. The authors note that raw parameter count is an imperfect complexity measure but do not recount it.

missing.what: OOD1 (extrapolation) error vs parameter count for m-PCE and DeepONet
Parameter range and per-point values of the m-PCE and DeepONet size sweeps, and m-PCE error at the authors' N line

record.verdict_notes: The interpolation threshold is the authors' np vs N count, with N = realizations × time steps. A per-regression count (basis terms vs input realizations) moves it by a factor of nt. Under that count the m-PCE optimum in Fig. 4 lies below threshold, which is why F1 is left undetermined. The V3 challenge holds under both counts but rests on a coarse doubling grid. The m-PCE fit may include a ridge/LASSO penalty (Eq. 12, unspecified), which would damp any peak. The text quotes the DeepONet best error as 2.95%, while Table 2 gives 2.85%. The four omitted Table 3 entries (130,796 → 2.952; 113,660 → 3.079; 99,900 → 3.246; 117,036 → 3.193) also mostly show smaller nets doing worse. Reader tranche T2 changed to T3. The reader's V1/V4 challenges were removed because DeepONet never approaches the threshold.

versions.untested_parts: The reported size sweep is for Case I DeepONet; the study does not test a fall-rise-fall curve across other deep networks or settings.
The study does not locate a peak or interpolation threshold along the sample-size axis, so it does not isolate the behavior specifically near that threshold.
The study tests parameter-count trends for m-PCE and DeepONet in Case I, not a broad range of model classes or the full classical U-shaped-to-double-descent transition.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.

The study does not test label-noise-driven peaks, multiple descent, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes such peaks. It reports input-noise robustness and some L2 regularization results, not this claim.
The study does not re-count complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that changes the curve into an ordinary U.

rows.value: figure only; text says error is minimized at approximately 22,320 parameters and subsequently increases as parameter count increases
rows.note: The reported trend has an error minimum followed by an increase; the text does not report a later second decrease.
rows.check: Figure only, and the sweep range is not readable. The authors place the over/under threshold at N=16,000, counting realizations × time steps. Per Eq. 22, np = basis size × dout, so the O m-PCE optimum (22,320) is about 496 basis terms against 800 input realizations. On that count it sits below the fitting threshold, and the later rise could be a first ascent rather than the absence of a second descent.

relation.reason: Its own generalization-error sweeps bear on the claims about model size and training-set size.

tranche.reason: The study reports its own model-size and sample-size results for Brusselator PDE surrogates, introducing a new setting rather than reproducing the original experiments or explicitly targeting double descent.

source_check.notes: The row states describe no observed worsening on the sampled grid; they do not establish absence near an actual interpolation threshold. The supplied text is the March 2022 arXiv v1 preprint.

statements.correction: Case I, Table 5: Under. m-PCE, 100 × nt: 5.75 ± 0.02%; 200 × nt: 5.68 ± 0.03%. Over. m-PCE, 400 × nt: 4.62 ± 0.03%; 800 × nt: 4.03 ± 0.02%; 1600 × nt: 3.69 ± 0.01%. Parameter-count crossings are bracketed; an actual interpolation threshold is not demonstrated. Section 2.2.1 specifies penalized least squares without establishing the penalty used for these results.
statements.problem: The m-PCE values and decreasing sampled errors are correct. Calling the parameter-count crossings identified fitting thresholds, and treating them as a demonstrated V3 challenge, overstates the evidence: training interpolation is not established and the coarse grid can miss a local peak. Claims about separate studies are outside this check.
